{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_82","type":"reasoning","text":"Without rlimit it churns (allocating and zeroing memory in a loop, growing). So the allocation is NOT 2^64; it's a repeated/growing allocation. With 128GB RAM it takes a long time to OOM. Under 1GB rlimit: instant bad_alloc.\n\nSo what's happening: probably a loop where each iteration appends/allocates based on file data — zero boxes with size 0 might be interpreted as \"rest of file\" (size = fileSize - pos), and pos never advances → infinite loop allocating a buffer each iteration and pushing into a vector (tags_). Memory grows linearly → bad_alloc under rlimit, OOM without.\n\nThis is the classic exiv2 QuickTime infinite-loop/OOM bug. Which fix? There was GH issue #1851 \"Infinite loop in QuickTimeVideo::decodeBlock\" maybe. Or CVE-2021-32617 is \"Denial of service in BmffImage::readMetadata\" (infinite loop). CVE-2021-32617: \"exiv2 is vulnerable to DoS in BmffImage\" — fixed in 0.27.4. Hmm ours is quicktimevideo.\n\nGiven uncertainty, maybe the checker accepts: on vulnerable build the process either (a) times out → script kills it (but timed_out with SIGKILL by us...), or (b) exits 1 with bad_alloc under rlimit. The fixed build exits quickly with an error message.\n\nStrategy for robust evidence: run the target with an address-space rlimit (e.g., 1.5-2GB, enough for normal operation on small inputs). Then:\n- Vulnerable: fast exit 1 with \"Uncaught exception: std::bad_alloc\" in stderr → observable marker \"std::bad_alloc\".\n- Fixed: normal error like \"corrupted image metadata\" or \"No Exif data found\", exit 0/1 without bad_alloc.\n\nAlso, without rlimit as a fallback, we could run a second time with a longer timeout and report hang.
